Gujarat High Court
Dhanjibhai Jadavjibhai Rathod vs State Of Gujarat on 11 July, 2016
Author:
P.P.Bhatt
Bench:
P.P.Bhatt
R/CR.MA/12833/2016                                                ORDER




                   IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

         CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR REGULAR BAIL) NO. 12833 of 2016
         ==========================================================
                   DHANJIBHAI JADAVJIBHAI RATHOD....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus
                        STATE OF GUJARAT....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR CHETAN K PANDYA, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1
         MR. JAY M THAKKAR, ADVOCATE for the Original Complainant;
         MR JK SHAH, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE P.P.BHATT

                                      Date : 11/07/2016


                                       ORAL ORDER
1.    The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of

         Criminal Procedure by the applicant for regular bail in connection with

         First Information Report being C.R.No.I-133/2016 registered with "A"
Division Police Station, Rajkot for the offences punishable under
Section

         304
of the Indian Penal Code.
2.    Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Public

         Prosecutor for the respondent-State as well as learned counsel for the

         original complainant.
Page 1 of 10
HC-NIC                                   Page 1 of 10     Created On Fri Jul 15 01:02:03 IST 2016
                     R/CR.MA/12833/2016                                               ORDER
3.   Learned advocate for the applicant has made following

         submissions:
(i)        that the applicant is working as Nursing Assistant in

              Saurashtra Stone Clinic and Research Institute Private Limited;
(ii)       that the action of the applicant was not with the intention to

              cause death or to cause such bodily injury as it likely to cause death

              nor the same was with knowledge that it was likely to cause death;
(iii)      that without admitting allegations made by the prosecution

              even if the allegations are taken their face value then also

              applicant's action be classified as rash or negligent on account of

              the fact that the preparatory medications were administered before

              the doctor comes;
(iv)       that no case is made out against the applicant under
Section

              304
of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, however, the applicant has

              been falsely implicated in the alleged offence;
(v)        that the applicant has not committed any offence as alleged

              in the FIR and the applicant has unblemished/dotless career as a

              Nursing Assistant and during his entire career, there has never been

              any instance or accusation of negligence and/or inquiry or

              punishment. It is also submitted that the applicant is sought to be

              involved in the false case;
(vi)       considering the FIR and documents produced by the
Page 2 of 10
HC-NIC                                     Page 2 of 10     Created On Fri Jul 15 01:02:03 IST 2016
            R/CR.MA/12833/2016                                               ORDER
applicant, no prima facie case is made out against the applicant for

         committing alleged offence;
(vii) that the applicant has cooperated with the Investigating

         Officer and shall make himself available as and when called by

         them.
(viii) that the applicant has deep roots in the society and thus will

         not jump the bail and the applicant will make himself available for

         the investigation if required and called by the Investigating Officer.
Learned counsel, upon instructions received from his client,

         submits that without prejudice to the rights and contentions of the

         applicant as well as hospital, the Director of the Hospital shall

         deposit Rs.7 lacs within two weeks from the date of release of the

         applicant. Undertaking to this effect will be filed by the Director of

         the said hospital before the concerned Trial Court while exercising

         the bail bond of the applicant.
(ix)    that they have no objection if the said amount is paid to the

         parents of the deceased-boy, but the said amount may be adjusted

         against any other claim put forward by the deceased family

         members either in Civil Court or Consumer Forum or any other

         Forum;
(x)     that substantial part of investigation is over by now,

         therefore, there is no possibility of tampering with the evidence.
Page 3 of 10
HC-NIC                            Page 3 of 10     Created On Fri Jul 15 01:02:03 IST 2016
            R/CR.MA/12833/2016                                                   ORDER
Learned counsel has referred to and relied upon the decision given in

         the case of
Mahadev Prasad Kaushik Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh

         and another
reported in (2008) 14 SCC 479 and submitted that
the

         said decision
is applicable to the facts and circumstances of the present

         case as almost similar situation is prevailing in the present case. The

         learned advocate for the applicant has referred relevant paragraphs

         of the judgment which are reproduced hereinbelow:
"22. Before
Section 304
can be invoked, the following ingredients must
          be satisfied;
(i) the death of the person must have been caused;
(ii) such death must have been caused by the act of the accused by
          causing bodily injury;
(iii) there must be an intention on the part of the accused
(a) to cause death; or
(b) to cause such bodily injury which is likely to cause death; (Part I)
(iv) there must be knowledge on the part of the accused that the bodily
          injury is such that it is likely to cause death (Part II).
23.
Section 304-A
was inserted by the
Indian Penal Code
          (Amendment) Act, 1870
and reads thus:
"304-A. Causing death by negligence.- Whoever causes the death
                 of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to
                 culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either
                 description for a term which may extend to two years, or with
                 fine, or with both."
The section deals with homicidal death by rash or negligent act. It does
          not create a new offence. It is directed against the offences outside the
Page 4 of 10
HC-NIC                               Page 4 of 10      Created On Fri Jul 15 01:02:03 IST 2016
           R/CR.MA/12833/2016                                                 ORDER



         range of
Sections 299
and
300
, IPC and covers those cases where death
         has been caused without 'intention' or 'knowledge'. The words "not
         amounting to culpable homicide" in the provision are significant and
         clearly convey that the section seeks to embrace those cases where there
         is neither intention to cause death, nor knowledge that the act done will
         in all probability result into death. It applies to acts which are rash or
         negligent and are directly the cause of death of another person.
24.   There is thus distinction between
Section 304
and
Section 304-A
.
Section 304-A
carves out cases where death is caused by doing a rash
         or negligent act which does not amount to culpable homicide not
         amounting to murder within the meaning of
Section 299
or culpable
         homicide amounting to murder under
Section 300
, IPC. In other words,
Section 304-A
excludes all the ingredients of
Section 299
as also of
Section 300
. Where intention or knowledge is the 'motivating force' of
         the act complained of,
Section 304-A
will have to make room for the
         graver and more serious charge of culpable homicide not amounting to
         murder or amounting to murder as the facts disclose. The section has
         application to those cases where there is neither intention to cause
         death nor knowledge that the act in all probability will cause death.
27.   The learned counsel for the appellant-accused submitted that by
         no stretch of imagination, it can be said that the appellant while
         administering injections to deceased Buddha Ram said to have
         committed an offence punishable under
Section 304
, IPC. It can never
         be said that the death of Buddha Ram had been caused by the appellant
         by doing the act of giving injections with intention to cause his death or
         to cause such bodily injury as is likely to cause death. Likewise, it is
         impossible to think that the purported act has been done by the
         appellant-accused with the knowledge that in all probability, it would
         result into the death of Buddha Ram.
Page 5 of 10
HC-NIC                            Page 5 of 10      Created On Fri Jul 15 01:02:03 IST 2016
           R/CR.MA/12833/2016                                                 ORDER
28.   In our opinion, the submission of the learned counsel for the
         appellant-accused is well-taken and deserves acceptance. Even if the
         averments made in the complaint are accepted in their entirety, the act
         in question of giving injections to deceased Buddha Ram would not fall
         within the mischief of
Section 304
, IPC. In our opinion, therefore, no
         process could have been issued against the appellant-accused for
         commission of an offence punishable under the said section. To that
         extent, therefore, the plea raised on behalf of the appellant must be
         upheld.
35.   In the circumstances, in our opinion, though on the facts and in
         the circumstances of the case, no summons could have been issued by
         the trial Court against the appellant for an offence punishable under
Section 304
, IPC, summons for an offence under
Section 304-A
, IPC
         ought to have been issued. The decisions on which strong reliance has
         been placed by the learned counsel for the appellant expressly allows
         such a step in certain circumstances, such as absence of possession of
         requisite skill or failure to exercise reasonable care by a professional.
         Nothing has been stated by the appellant about his qualifications or of
         'requisite skill' in the profession he was practising. There was also
         nothing to show that before administering injections, he had undertaken
         reasonable care ought to have been taken by a professional.
37.   On the facts of the case, ailment of Buddha Ram prima facie could
         not be said to be of such a serious nature which would result in death
         during his treatment. The allegation of the complainant which has been
         corroborated by statements of other eye-witnesses is that immediately
         after administration of three injections, the colour of the body of Buddha
         Ram turned into blue and within half an hour he died.If in the light of
         the above facts and circumstances, proceedings have been initiated
Page 6 of 10
HC-NIC                            Page 6 of 10      Created On Fri Jul 15 01:02:03 IST 2016
                      R/CR.MA/12833/2016                                                ORDER



                against the appellant for an offence punishable under
Section 304A
, IPC
                (though not under
Section 304
, IPC), it cannot be said that no such
                action could be taken. We are, therefore, of the view that submission on
                behalf of the learned counsel for the complainant deserves to be
                accepted to the above extent.
38.       For the foregoing reasons, in our judgment, the appeal deserves to
                be partly allowed. So far as issuance of process for offences punishable
                under
Sections 504
and
506
, IPC is concerned, it is liable to be quashed
                and is hereby quashed. Likewise, process for an offence punishable
                under
Section 304
, IPC is ill-conceived on the facts of the case and the
                process could only be issued by the learned Magistrate to the appellant-
                accused for an offence punishable under
Section 304-A
, IPC. The
                appeal is accordingly allowed to the extent indicated above."
The learned advocate for the applicant while considering his

               arguments submitted that considering
the above decision
of the

               Hon'ble Supreme Court and considering the nature and gravity of

               the offence and the role attributed to the applicant, the applicant

               may be enlarged on regular bail by imposing suitable conditions.
4.    Learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent-State as

         well as learned counsel for the original complainant have opposed the

         application for grant of regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of

         the offence. They have further submitted that there is a prima facie case

         against the present applicant. Therefore, the present application may be

         rejected.
Page 7 of 10
HC-NIC                                       Page 7 of 10     Created On Fri Jul 15 01:02:03 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/12833/2016                                               ORDER
5.      Regard being had to the above submissions, in the facts and

         circumstances of the case and considering the nature and gravity of

         accusation made against the applicant in the First Information Report and

         other police papers as well as considering the
ratio
laid down in
the

         aforesaid decision, this Court is of the opinion that discretion is required to

         be exercised in favour of the applicant for grant of bail as substantial part

         of investigation is over, therefore, now there is no possibility of

         tampering with the evidence. Hence, the present application is allowed

         and the applicant is ordered to be released on regular bail in connection

         with the FIR being C.R.No.I-133/2016 registered with "A" Division

         Police Station, Rajkot on his executing a personal bond of Rs.10,000/-
(Rupees Ten Thousand Only) with one local surety of the like amount to

         the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court, and subject to the following

         conditions, that the applicant shall;
[a]     not take undue advantage of liberty or misuse liberty;
                [b]    not act in a manner injurious to the interest of the
                       prosecution;
[c]    surrender passport, if any, to the lower court within a week;
                [d]    not leave the State of Gujarat without prior permission of the
                       Sessions Judge concerned;
[e]    mark presence before the concerned Police Station on every
                       Monday of each English calendar month for a period of
                       three months and thereafter, alternate Monday for a period
                       of six months, between 11:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m.;
Page 8 of 10
HC-NIC                                   Page 8 of 10     Created On Fri Jul 15 01:02:03 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/12833/2016                                                 ORDER



               [f]    furnish latest and permanent address of residence to the
Investigating Officer, and also to the Court at the time of
                      execution of the bond, and shall not change the residence
                      without prior permission of this Court;
[g]    deposit an amount of Rs.7 lacs before the concerned Trial
                      Court within one week from the date of release of the
                      applicant failing which this order shall not operate and the
                      Nazir Department of the concerned Trial Court shall
                      disburse the said amount in favour of the parents of the
                      deceased-boy by account payee cheque after proper
                      verification. In the event of filing any proceedings before the
                      learned Civil Court or Consumer Forum or any other
                      mediation       proceedings,       the    said       amount         shall      be
                      adjusted/deducted against the decree/compromise deed that
                      may be passed/arrived at between the parties in future in
                      respect of compensation claim, if any.
6.    The authorities will release the applicant only if he is not required

         in connection with any other offence for the time being. If breach of any

         of the above conditions is committed, the Sessions Judge concerned will

         be free to issue warrant or take appropriate action in the matter. Bail

         bond to be executed before the learned Lower Court having jurisdiction

         to try the case. It will be open for the concerned Court to delete, modify

         and/or relax any of the above conditions, in accordance with law. At the

         trial, learned trial court shall not be influenced by the observations of

         preliminary nature, qua the evidence at this stage made by this Court

         while enlarging the applicant on bail.
Page 9 of 10
HC-NIC                                    Page 9 of 10     Created On Fri Jul 15 01:02:03 IST 2016
                     R/CR.MA/12833/2016                                              ORDER
7.       Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent. Direct service is

         permitted.
(P.P.BHATT, J.)
         rakesh

Gujarat High Court
Punabhai Rambhai Jogasva vs State Of Gujarat on 29 December, 2016
Author:
C.L.Soni
Bench:
C.L. Soni
R/CR.MA/33831/2016                                                 ORDER




                   IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

          CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR ANTICIPATORY BAIL ) NO. 33831
                                              of 2016

         ================================================================
                         PUNABHAI RAMBHAI JOGASVA....Applicant(s)
                                        Versus
                            STATE OF GUJARAT....Respondent(s)
         ================================================================
         Appearance:
         MR ASHISH M DAGLI, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1
         MR H S SONI, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ================================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE C.L. SONI

                                        Date : 29/12/2016


                                         ORAL ORDER
[1]   By way of the present application under
Section 438
of the
         Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ('the Code'), the applicant has
         prayed to release him on bail in case of his arrest in connection with
         the FIR being I-CR NO. 132 of 2016 registered with Gondal City
         Police   Station,        District:   Rajkot        (Rural)         for    the      offences
         punishable under
Sections 302
,
307
,
506(2)
,
120(b)
and
34
of the
         Indian Penal Code and
Section 25
(1-B), A and 27 of the
Arms Act
and
Section 135
of the Gujarat Police Act.
[2]   Mr Dagli, learned advocate for the applicant submitted that the
         applicant is not alleged to have played any role in the matter of
         commission of offence of murder. He submitted that the applicant is
         sought to be involved in the offence alleged just on suspicion that he
         harbored one person at his farm-house who was alleged to have
         committed the offence of murder with other persons. He has
         submitted that in absence of any material when the applicant is
Page 1 of 4
HC-NIC                                    Page 1 of 4       Created On Fri Dec 30 00:25:07 IST 2016
                  R/CR.MA/33831/2016                                             ORDER



         sought to be involved in the serious offence like 302, and considering
         the   allegation made in the FIR, no custodial interrogation of the
         applicant    is required and, therefore, the Court may exercise
         discretion in favour of the applicant under Section 438 of the Code.
[3]   Mr. H S Soni, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the
         respondent - State submitted that during the investigation in
         connection with the FIR it is found from the statements of the
         employees working with the applicant that one co-accused named
         Haneef was given shelter for about ten days by the applicant after
         commission of the offence alleged in the FIR. He submitted that the
         accused whose presence was otherwise required for interrogation in
         connection with the offence as alleged in the FIR, when was harbored
         by the applicant, the applicant's complexity in the offence alleged is
         to be found out and therefore, the interrogation of the applicant is
         required. He therefore, urged that since the investigation is in
         progress, the Court may not exercise the discretion in favour of the
         applicant under section 438 of the Code.
[4]   The Court, having heard the learned advocates for both the
         sides and having considered the nature of the allegations in the FIR
         with the police papers and having considered, finds that though the
         offences alleged are as regards the commission of murder of a
         person, however, from the material collected by the Police and as
         pointed out by the learned APP Mr. Soni except that the applicant had
         allowed co-accused Haneef to stay at his farm-house at the request of
         the friend of Haneef, the applicant is not alleged to have committed
         any further act with other accused in committing the offence of
         murder and having considered the statement of co-accused Haneef
         dated 12.09.2016, the discretion deserves to be exercised under
         Section 438 of the Code in favour of the applicant.
[5]   In the result, the present application is allowed. It is ordered
         that in case the applicant is arrested in connection with FIR being I-
Page 2 of 4
HC-NIC                                Page 2 of 4      Created On Fri Dec 30 00:25:07 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/33831/2016                                                 ORDER
CR NO. 132 of 2016 registered with Gondal City Police Station,
         District: Rajkot (Rural) he shall be released on bail on his
         furnishing a personal bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousands
         only) with one surety of like amount, on the following conditions that
         he :
(a)    shall cooperate with the investigation and make himself
                available for interrogation whenever required;
(b)    shall remain present at the concerned Police Station on
                05/01/2017 between 11:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m.;
(c)    shall not misuse his liberty;
         (d)    shall not obstruct or hamper the police investigation and not to
play mischief with the evidence collected or yet to be collected
                by the Police;
(e)    shall at the time of execution of bond, furnish the address to
                the Investigating Officer and the Court concerned and shall not
                change his        residence till the final disposal of the case or till
                further orders;
(f)    shall not leave India without the permission of the Court and, if
                having passports shall surrender the same before the Trial
                Court within a week.
[6]    This order shall not be construed to divest the Investigating
         Agency to ask for remand of the applicant if required. In such case,
         the applicant shall remain present before the learned Magistrate on
         the first date of hearing of such application and on all subsequent
         occasions, as may be directed by the learned Magistrate. This would
         be sufficient to treat the accused in the judicial custody for the
         purpose of entertaining application of the prosecution for police
         remand. This is, however, without prejudice to the right of the
         accused to seek stay against an order of remand, if ultimately
         granted, and the power of the learned Magistrate to consider such a
         request in accordance with law. It is clarified that the applicant, even
Page 3 of 4
HC-NIC                                     Page 3 of 4      Created On Fri Dec 30 00:25:07 IST 2016
                    R/CR.MA/33831/2016                                             ORDER



         if, remanded to the police custody, upon completion of such period of
         police remand, shall be set free immediately, subject to other
         conditions of this anticipatory bail order.
[7]    At the trial, the Trial Court shall not be influenced by the prima
         facie observations made by this Court while enlarging the applicant
         on bail. Rule is made absolute. The present application is disposed of
         accordingly.
Direct service is permitted.
(C.L.SONI, J.)

Gujarat High Court
Dharmesh @ Bhodi Raijibhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 5 August, 2016
Author:
C.L.Soni
Bench:
C.L. Soni
R/CR.MA/17028/2016                                              ORDER




                  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

          CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR ANTICIPATORY BAIL ) NO. 17028
                                            of 2016

         ==========================================================
                   DHARMESH @ BHODI RAIJIBHAI PATEL....Applicant(s)
                                     Versus
                        STATE OF GUJARAT....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR NITIN T GANDHI, ADVOCATE for the Applicant(s) No. 1
         MRS. HANSA PUNANI APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================

          CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE C.L. SONI

                                      Date : 05/08/2016


                                       ORAL ORDER
[1]   The present is the successive application filed 

         under
Section 438
of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 

         1973,   ("the   Code"),   seeking   anticipatory   bail   in 

         connection   with   the  FIR   being     I­CR   NO.   6   of   2016 

         registered   with  Virpur   Police   Station,   Dist.­ 

         Mahisagar  for the offences punishable under
Sections 

         302
,
201
,
323
,
120B
, and
114
of the Indian Penal Code 

         ('the Code'). The first application for anticipatory 

         bail was permitted to be withdrawn by this Court vide 

         order dated 14/06/2016.
Page 1 of 8
HC-NIC                                  Page 1 of 8      Created On Tue Aug 09 03:01:40 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/17028/2016                                            ORDER



         [2]         The   present   application   is   filed   mainly   on
the   ground   that   in   the   charge­sheet,   now   filed   the 

         applicant is shown to be the panch­witness.



         [3]         To   oppose   the   application,   affidavit­in­

         reply   is   filed   by   Mr.   Vinay   Shukla,   Deputy 

         Superintendent of Police, Lunavada, Mahisagar  wherein 

         it is explained as to why the applicant was referred 

         as panch­witness in the charge­sheet.



         [4]         Learned   advocate   Mr.   Gandhi   for   the 

         applicant   submitted   that   the   applicant   was   in   fact 

         called up to be the panch­witness by the police as the 

         applicant   was   not   found   involved   in   the   offences 

         alleged.   Mr.   Gandhi   submitted   that   when   the   first 

         application was made, the applicant had presented his 

         case based on the contents of the FIR, so as to argue 

         that the applicant has not committed any offence.  Mr. 

         Gandhi   submitted   that   during   the   investigation,   the 

         applicant   is   not   found   to   have   played   any   role   to 

         commit murder of deceased person and therefore, this 

         Court   can   consider   the   successive   anticipatory   bail 

         application   on   filing   the   charge­sheet.   Mr.   Gandhi
Page 2 of 8
HC-NIC                               Page 2 of 8      Created On Tue Aug 09 03:01:40 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/17028/2016                                            ORDER



         submitted   that   even   as   per   the   charge­sheet,   the 

         applicant is shown to be one of the panch witnesses 

         and   simply   alleged   to   have   accompanied   the   other 

         accused   and   therefore   considering   the   charge­sheet 

         papers   the   Court   may   entertain   this   successive 

         application   for   anticipatory   bail.   Mr.   Gandhi   has 

         relied some decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court and of 

         different High Courts, so as to point out that there 

         is  prohibition for considering the anticipatory bail 

         at   any   stage   before   arrest   and   even   after   charge­

         sheet,   if   it   is   found   that   the   applicant   deserves 

         grant of anticipatory bail.
[5]         Learned   APP   Mrs.   Punani   drew   attention   of 

         the Court to the affidavit­in­reply and submitted that 

         since the affidavit explains the circumstances under 

         which the applicant was shown to be panch­witness in 

         charge­sheet,   though   he   is   one   of   the   accused 

         responsible   for   committing   murder   of   deceased,   this 

         Court   may   not   consider   this   successive   anticipatory 

         bail application of the applicant.
[6]         The   Court,   having   heard   learned   advocates
Page 3 of 8
HC-NIC                               Page 3 of 8      Created On Tue Aug 09 03:01:40 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/17028/2016                                            ORDER
for both the sides and having perused the charge­sheet 

         with   affidavit­in­reply   filed   by   the   Deputy 

         Superintendent   of   Police,   finds   that   in   the   second 

         column  of the charge­sheet, the applicant is shown to 

         be absconding person. In the last column of   charge­

         sheet  the   applicant   is   shown   to   have   conspired   with 

         other   accused   for   commission   of   offences   alleged   in 

         the   F.I.R.   However,   in   the   third   column   of   charge­

         sheet, the applicant is shown to be one of the panch­

         witnesses.   In   paragraph   No.3   of   the   affidavit­in­

         reply,   the   deponent   has   explained   the   circumstances 

         under which the applicant was shown to be  one of the 

         panch witnesses as under:­

               " In response to petitioner contention raised by  
               petition   I   say   that   accidental   death   No.10/15  
               has   been   registered     before   Virpur   Police  
               Station on 12.08.2015 at 13/30, where in it has  
               been declared by one Shri Shaileshbhai Rajivbhai  
               Patel that dead body of one male person is found  
               near   Ratankaa,   sim   of   Varghara   village,  
               immediately inquiry was carried out by concerned  
               Police Station and Inquest panchnama was carried  
               out on 12.02.2015, on the same day, I say that 
               his  name  was  shown   as one  of  the  panch­witness  
               in   the   inquest   panchnama   and   thereforein   the  
               charge   sheet  his  name  has  been   shown  as  panch­
               witness, at that time his name was not disclosed  
               as   accused   or   suspect.   I   say   that   after  
               investigation, as there was ample evidence, his  
               name  is    disclosed   as accused  and  therefore  no  
               malafide   intention   by   investigation   agency,   he  
               has   been   shown   as   accused   therefore   contention  
               raised   by petition   is baseless   and  it does   not  
               vitiate any investigation or prosecution case, I  
               further say that this anticipatory Bail deserves
Page 4 of 8
HC-NIC                               Page 4 of 8      Created On Tue Aug 09 03:01:40 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/17028/2016                                             ORDER



               to   be   rejected   as   his   active   role   has   been  
               disclosed in F.I.R while committing offence and  
               his presence is proved, I further say that this  
               is   successive   bail   application   and   there   is   no  
               change of circumstance. This Hon'ble High Court  
               &   learned   Sessions   Court   has   also   rejected   his  
               anticipatory Bail application on merits, also he  
               has not surrender himself and in charge sheet he  
               has been shown as absconder, even under
Section  
               70
of   Criminal   Procedure   Code,   proceeding   have  
               been initiated again him".
[7]         The   Court   finds   in   view   of   the   above 

         circumstances   pointed   out   in   the   affidavit­in­reply, 

         it could not be accepted that the applicant was just 

         panch­witness   and   not   involvement   in   the   offences 

         alleged in the FIR. If the applicant was just panch 

         witness to the Inquest panchnama, he was not required 

         to be shown in concise details in the last column with 

         other   accused   alleging   conspiracy   to   commit   serious 

         crime   like   murder.   Therefore,   simply   because   the 

         applicant was taken as a panch­witness at the initial 

         stage would not be a ground available to the applicant 

         to urge that he is not involved in offences alleged in 

         the F.I.R. The Court, therefore, finds that filing of 

         charge­sheet   by   describing   the   applicant   as   panch 

         witness   on   the   basis   of   the   Inquest   Panchnama   made 

         when the offences were not disclosed would not be the 

         change   in   the   circumstances   for   entertaining   the
Page 5 of 8
HC-NIC                                Page 5 of 8      Created On Tue Aug 09 03:01:40 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/17028/2016                                            ORDER



         successive anticipatory bail application. Now when the 

         investigation has been done and it is found that the 

         applicant was equally involved with other accused for 

         commission   of   the  crime  alleged   in   the  FIR,   showing 

         the   name   of   the   applicant   as   panch­witness   in   the 

         charge­sheet would not make any difference and cannot 

         be a ground to exercise the discretion under
section 

         438
of   the   Code.   Mr.   Gandhi   however   relied   on   the 

         judgments in the case of
Ravindra Saxena Vs. State of 

         Rajasthan
2010   (1)   G.L.H.382   (SC),  in   the   case   of
I.Y.   Chanda   Earappa   Vs.   State   of   Karnataka
,   1989 

         CRI.L.J.   2405,  in   the   case   of
Jitubhai   Shanabhai 

         Bhatt   Vs.   State   of   Gujarat
1992(3)   Crimes   147,  and 

         other judgments of different High Courts to point out 

         that the  anticipatory bail can be granted even after 

         the   filing   chalan   (charge­sheet)   and   there   is   no 

         prohibition   for   grant   of   anticipatory   bail   at   any 

         stage   before   the   arrest   is   made   even   in   connection 

         with the offences under
Section 302
of the Code.   As 

         per the above judgment, though successive anticipatory 

         bail   applications   could   be   filed   after   the   charge­

         sheet, however the Court is to decide to exercise the 

         discretion jurisdiction in the facts of the case.
Page 6 of 8
HC-NIC                               Page 6 of 8      Created On Tue Aug 09 03:01:40 IST 2016
                 R/CR.MA/17028/2016                                            ORDER




         [8]         In the present case, change in circumstances
pointed out is that the applicant is shown as the one 

         of the panch­wintess. Mr. Gandhi though attempted to 

         argue   that   there   is   no   evidence   to   involve   the 

         applicant   in   the   offences,   however   the   Court   finds 

         that based on the theory of conspiracy the applicant 

         is   shown   to   have   been   equally   involved   in   the 

         commission of serious crime. The case was   initially 

         registered   as   accidental   death   case   and   then   with 

         progress   of   investigation,   the   involvement   of   the 

         applicant was found. However, as per the primary stage 

         of procedure, the applicant was taken as panch witness 

         when   accidental   death   was   registered.     The   name   of 

         applicant   as   panch­witness   continued   in   the   charge­

         sheet.   But   such   would   not   make   any   difference   when 

         investigation revealed that the applicant was found to 

         have conspired for commission of the offences alleged. 

         In   connection   with   such   offences,   the   police   might 

         require   custodial   interrogation   of   the   applicant 

         especially   for   the   recovery   of   the   motorcycle   bike 

         alleged to have been used by the applicant to complete 

         the chain of the events. Therefore, in the facts and
Page 7 of 8
HC-NIC                               Page 7 of 8      Created On Tue Aug 09 03:01:40 IST 2016
                   R/CR.MA/17028/2016                                            ORDER



         circumstances   of   the   case,   and   considering   the 

         concise   details   mentioned   in   the  last   column  of  the 

         charge­sheet showing that the applicant was involved 

         with other accused in the commission of the offences 

         alleged   and  shown  to  be  absconding,  the   Court   finds 

         that   the   present   successive   anticipatory   bail 

         application   is   not   required   to   be   entertained.   The 

         application, is therefore, rejected.
(C.L.SONI, J.)
         MANOJ KUMAR

Gujarat High Court
State Of Gujarat vs Dinesh Jivabhai Gagiya & ... on 13 June, 2016
Author:
R.P.Dholaria
Bench:
R.P.Dholaria
R/CR.A/2204/2005                                                    JUDGMENT




                     IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

                               CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 2204 of 2005


         FOR APPROVAL AND SIGNATURE:


         HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE R.P.DHOLARIA

         ==========================================================

         1     Whether Reporters of Local Papers may be allowed to see the
               judgment ?

         2     To be referred to the Reporter or not ?

         3     Whether their Lordships wish to see the fair copy of the
               judgment ?

         4     Whether this case involves a substantial question of law as to
               the interpretation of the Constitution of India or any order made
               thereunder ?

         ==========================================================
                            STATE OF GUJARAT....Appellant(s)
                                       Versus
                 DINESH JIVABHAI GAGIYA & 1....Opponent(s)/Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         MR LR PUJARI, APP for the Appellant(s) No. 1
         MR PRADIP J PATEL, ADVOCATE for the Opponent(s)/Respondent(s) No. 1
         -2
         ==========================================================

             CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE R.P.DHOLARIA

                                            Date : 13/06/2016

                                            ORAL JUDGMENT
1.             The          appellant           State          of        Gujarat                 has
         preferred the present appeal under
section 378(1)
         (3)
of     the         Code    of      Criminal             Procedure,                1973
         against the judgment and order of acquittal dated
         15.5.2004 rendered by learned Additional Sessions
Page 1 of 8
HC-NIC                                        Page 1 of 8       Created On Fri Jun 17 01:41:42 IST 2016
                  R/CR.A/2204/2005                                                    JUDGMENT



         Judge,       Fast          Track    Court,           Junagadh            in       Sessions
         Case No.61 of 2003.
2.            The          short    facts            giving           rise          to          the
         present appeal are that the complainant lodged
         the complaint stating the fact that on 6.1.2003
         at    about        12.00       pm     when           she      was        sleeping                at
         residence with her parents, at that time, Praful
         Bachu,       Jagesh          Chavda       and        Dinesh          Jiva         who           are
         neighbours           of      the    complainant                 came         there              and
         knocked the door of the house. It is alleged that
         all the three persons were giving filthy abuses
         and hence, she woke up from her sleep. It is
         alleged that at that time, the said persons were
         quarreling           with      her        father           and        accused             No.2
         snatched her out and took her to nearby street
         with     an     intention           to      commit           rape         on      her           and
         thereafter assaulted her and torn her cloth. It
         is     alleged         that,        therefore,               she         shouted                and
         accused No.2 fled away. Hence, the complaint came
         to be lodged against the respondents accused.
3.            In       pursuance            of        the        complaint,                     the
         Investigating                 Officer                 carried                out                the
         investigation and filed the chargesheet against
         the respondents accused. The charge was framed
         against        the         accused.        The        accused            pleaded                not
         guilty to the charge and claimed to be tried.
3.1           In order to bring home the guilt, the
         prosecution            has     examined           5     witnesses               and       also
Page 2 of 8
HC-NIC                                       Page 2 of 8       Created On Fri Jun 17 01:41:42 IST 2016
                 R/CR.A/2204/2005                                                  JUDGMENT



         produced       documentary           evidences              such         as      medical
         certificate of injury to the complainant                                         Exh.13,
Yadi to PI for investigation of offence Exh.24,
         copy of the complaint Exh.25, original complaint
         of the complainant Exh.15 etc.


         3.2          At the end of the trial, after recording
         the statements of the accused under
section 313
of the CrPC and hearing the arguments on behalf
         of the prosecution and the defence, learned trial
         Court delivered the judgment and order, as stated
         above.
4.           Being          aggrieved              by       the         same,                the
         appellant          State      has       preferred                the        aforesaid
         Criminal Appeal before this Court.
5.           By way of preferring the present appeal,
         the appellant has mainly contended that learned
         trial Court has failed to appreciate the evidence
         on    record        and     wrongly           recorded            the        order           of
         acquittal. It is further contended that learned
         trial Judge has not appreciated the evidence on
         record in its proper perspective and in fact,
         there was no appreciation of evidence so far and
         hence,       the          impugned       judgment              and         order             of
         acquittal is required to be reversed, as such.
5.1          Mr.L.R.Pujari, learned APP appearing for
         the appellant State has reiterated and urged the
         grounds mentioned in the memo of appeal. Learned
Page 3 of 8
HC-NIC                                   Page 3 of 8        Created On Fri Jun 17 01:41:42 IST 2016
                R/CR.A/2204/2005                                                   JUDGMENT



         APP has taken this Court through the paper-book
         and evidence on record and argued that learned
         trial Court failed to appreciate the evidence on
         record      and          wrongfully             acquitted            the         accused
         though ample evidence is available on record. In
         his   submission,             therefore,            learned           trial          Court
         ought to have convicted the accused and hence,
         learned trial Court has failed to appreciate the
         evidence       on        record      and         wrongly           recorded                  the
         judgment of acquittal which is required to be
         reversed and the respondents are required to be
         convicted, as such.
6.          On       the       other-hand,                Mr.Pradip                Patel,
         learned Advocate for the respondents accused has
         taken this Court through the entire evidence on
         record and submitted that the impugned judgment
         and order passed by the learned trial Judge is
         just and proper. Mr.Patel further submitted that
         in view of the evidence on record, it cannot be
         said that the learned trial Judge has committed
         any    error             in   passing              the       impugned                order
         acquitting          the       accused,             and        therefore,                     the
         present appeal deserves to be dismissed.
7.          This          Court       has          heard         Mr.L.R.Pujari,
         learned APP for the appellant State and Mr.Pradip
         Patel,      learned           advocate             for      the         respondents
         accused.
8.          This Court has minutely gone through the
         impugned judgment rendered by learned trial Court
Page 4 of 8
HC-NIC                                     Page 4 of 8      Created On Fri Jun 17 01:41:42 IST 2016
                  R/CR.A/2204/2005                                                     JUDGMENT



         as well as the evidence on record in the nature
         of paper book. As per the prosecution case, on
         6.1.2003          around        at        12.30            hours,            while               the
         complainant as well as witnesses were sleeping in
         their        houses,           at      that            time,            the          present
         respondents herein as well as one Praful Bachu
         (since        deceased)             knocked              the         door           of           the
         complainant's house and thereafter entered in the
         house and they were quarreling with the father of
         the complainant; at that time, respondent accused
         Jagesh Chavda dragged the complainant in order to
         outrage her modesty and assaulted her and torn
         her cloth and on shouting by the complainant, the
         accused fled away from the place of incident.
8.1           It      is     pertinent            to      note         that        for           the
         same incident, counter complaint was also lodged
         prior to the present complaint around at 3.25
         hours      on      6.1.2003          respondent                  Dinesh            Jivabhai
         Gagiya has lodged the complaint alleging that the
         father and two brothers-in-law and one unknown
         person       have          committed        murder            of      Praful           Bachu.
         Therefore, at the time of lodging the complaint,
         accused No.1 Praful Bachu was already died and,
         therefore,           after      conclusion                  of       investigation,
         chargesheet            was     filed        against             the       present                two
         respondents.
8.2           In order to prove the case against the
         accused, the prosecution has examined 5 witnesses
         and     also        produced           documentary                   evidences.                   PW
Page 5 of 8
HC-NIC                                       Page 5 of 8        Created On Fri Jun 17 01:41:42 IST 2016
                 R/CR.A/2204/2005                                                      JUDGMENT



         Jaishreeben i.e. victim has been examined and she
         has deposed as per the allegations made in her
         complaint.           In her deposition, she has narrated
         the incident occurred as the present respondents
         as well as deceased Praful Bachu threatened her
         to kidnap and commit rape on her. However, during
         the course of her deposition, she has narrated
         that incident occurred as her mother Jaya lend
         money keeping surety of golden ring and though
         the    amount             was     returned,                accused             were              not
         returning golden ring, due to which incident took
         place. PW 3 Jayaben - mother of the victim has
         been examined as witness. She has also narrated
         the same thing in examination-in-chief, but in
         her cross examination, she has admitted that as
         she    was       sleeping,              incident              took         place           and,
         therefore, she did not know anything as regards
         to happening of the incident.
8.3          Except             the       aforesaid               two         witnesses,
         nothing       worth        is     coming            out      from         evidence                of
         other witnesses.
8.3          On overall analysis of the evidence on
         record, it is clear that the present complaint is
         counter blast in order to avoid charges of murder
         of one Praful Bachu whose murder was committed in
         the house of the present complainant during the
         same hours on 6.1.2003 at about 12.30 hours for
         which against the father of the complainant as
         well    as      two        brothers-in-law                    and         one        unknown
Page 6 of 8
HC-NIC                                         Page 6 of 8      Created On Fri Jun 17 01:41:42 IST 2016
                  R/CR.A/2204/2005                                                    JUDGMENT



         person, complaint came to be lodged.                                       In order to
         save      their            skin    from          that        prosecution,                       the
         present complaint appears to have been lodged.
         The evidence on record does not link the accused
         with the crime in question.                             Even, injury on the
         person of the complainant was found which was in
         the nature of self infliction as per the say of
         the     Doctor.            Under     the         circumstances,                     learned
         trial Court has rightly acquitted the respondents
         accused        considering           the         nature          of      evidence                on
         record.
9.            It is also a settled legal position that
         in acquittal appeals, the appellate Court is not
         required to rewrite the judgment or to give fresh
         reasonings,            when       the      reasons            assigned              by          the
         Court below are found to be just and proper.
10.           In above view of the matter, this Court
         is of the considered opinion that learned trial
         court was completely justified in acquitting the
         respondent of the charges leveled against him.
         This Court finds that the findings recorded by
         learned        trial         court        are         absolutely               just             and
         proper and in recording the said findings, no
         illegality or infirmity has been committed by it.
         This Court is, therefore, in complete agreement
         with the findings, ultimate conclusion and the
         resultant order of acquittal recorded by learned
         court      below           and     hence         finds           no       reasons               to
Page 7 of 8
HC-NIC                                      Page 7 of 8        Created On Fri Jun 17 01:41:42 IST 2016
                   R/CR.A/2204/2005                                              JUDGMENT



         interfere with the same.
11.            In      the   result,          this     appeal            fails             and
         accordingly, it is dismissed. Bail bond, if any,
         stands cancelled. R & P to be sent back to the
         trial Court, forthwith.
(R.P.DHOLARIA,J.)

Gujarat High Court
Mahendrasinh Pratapsinh Thakur vs State Of Gujarat & 3 on 21 January, 2016
Author:
J.B.Pardiwala
Bench:
J.B.Pardiwala
R/SCR.A/467/2015                                                   ORDER




                    IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD

              SPECIAL CRIMINAL APPLICATION (DIRECTION) NO. 467 of 2015

         ==========================================================
                    MAHENDRASINH PRATAPSINH THAKUR....Applicant(s)
                                      Versus
                        STATE OF GUJARAT & 3....Respondent(s)
         ==========================================================
         Appearance:
         PARTY-IN-PERSON, PERSONAL CAPACITY for the Applicant(s) No. 1
         NOTICE SERVED for the Respondent(s) No. 2 - 4
         MR JK SHAH, ADD. PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the Respondent(s) No. 1
         ==========================================================

                   CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE J.B.PARDIWALA
          
                                          Date : 21/01/2016 
                                            ORAL ORDER
1.     By this writ­application under
Article 226
of the Constitution of 
         India,   the   petitioner­original   first   informant,   father   of   the   deceased 
         prayed for the following reliefs:­

                "26(a) To allow this petition;
(b)    To   issue   a   writ   of   mandamus   and/or   any   other   appropriate  
                writ, order or direction transferring the investigation of FIR being C.R.  
                No.I­125/2014 registered with A Division Police Station, Himatnagar,  
                Sabarkantha   to   any   other   independent   agency   unconnected   with  
                present  investigating agency;
(c)     Pending admission, hearing and final disposal of this petition,  
                to direct the respondent no.2 to produce Action Taken Report (ATR) in  
                connection with the FIR being C.R. No.I­125/2014 registered with A  
                Division Police Station, Himatnagar, Sabarkantha;
(d)    To pass any other and further orders as may be deemed fit and  
                proper to this Hon'ble Court."
2.     It appears from the materials on record that the petitioner herein
Page 1 of 4
HC-NIC                                        Page 1 of 4       Created On Sat Jan 23 01:53:26 IST 2016
                     R/SCR.A/467/2015                                                 ORDER



         is a practicing advocate in Himmatnagar. On 26th September, 2014, his 
         son i.e. the deceased was in company of one Govindbhai. The deceased 
         alongwith   Govindbhai   and   one   another   person   were   travelling   on   a 
         motorcycle bearing Registration No.GJ­09­CH­0185. The motorcycle met 
         with   an   accident   with   a   tempo.   It   appears   that   the   person   who   was 
         driving the tempo fled away from the spot of the accident. Till this date, 
         the police has not been able to get any clue as regards the tempo as well 
         as the registered owner of that particular tempo. The accident proved to 
         be fatal so far as  the son of the petitioner herein is concerned. The two 
         other   persons   who   were   on   the   motorcycle   does   not   seem   to   have 
         sustained any injury. The postmortem was performed and the cause of 
         death is shown to be cardio­respiratory arrest on account of head injury.
3.     The F.I.R came to be registered for the offence punishable under 
         Sections­304(A) of the
I.P.C
. i.e. for rash and negligent act.
4.     The   petitioner   as   a   father   of   the   deceased   has   a   strong 
         apprehension that the case is not one of an accident but the same is of 
         murder. According to him, the investigation  has not proceeded in the 
         right direction. He therefore prays that the same be transferred to any 
         other independent agency.
5.     On the other hand, Mr. J.K. Shah, the learned APP appearing for 
         the State pointed out that the investigation has been carried out in the 
         right direction. The Investigating Officer has not been able to collect any 
         materials on the basis of which it could be said that the case is one of 
         murder.   According   to   Mr.   Shah,   the   statements   of   the   eye­witnesses 
         recorded goes to show that it was an accident.
6.     It appears that some statements under Section­164 of the Cr.P.C.
Page 2 of 4
HC-NIC                                       Page 2 of 4      Created On Sat Jan 23 01:53:26 IST 2016
                     R/SCR.A/467/2015                                                  ORDER
have also been recorded. It also appears that the Investigating Officer is 
         relying on the opinion given by the doctor that the injuries sustained by 
         the deceased could have been caused on account of such accident. I am 
         also told that few persons were subjected to the Lie Detection Test.
7.     Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and 
         having considered the materials on record, the only question that falls 
         for my consideration is whether the investigation should be transferred 
         to any independent agency.
8.     It appears that till this date, the Investigating Officer has not been 
         able to ascertain as regards the tempo involved in the so­called accident. 
         It   is   also   not   in   dispute   that   three   persons   were   travelling   on   the 
         motorcycle. It also appears from the statement that the deceased was 
         sitting in between the two other persons who were on the motorcycle.
9.     It   is   very   strange   that   in   the   so­called   accident   said   to   have 
         occurred two other persons who were on the motorcycle did not sustain 
         any   injury.   It   appears   that   very   minimal   damage   was   caused   to   the 
         motorcycle.   In   fact,   the   photographs   would   reveal   that   there   was   no 
         damage at all to the motorcycle. If that be so, then this entire theory of 
         accident appears to be unpalatable or rather doubtful. If the theory of 
         accident has to be ruled out for the time being, then probably there is 
         some substance in the apprehension expressed by the petitioner that the 
         case is one of murder.
10.    It also appears that after the accident, the deceased was taken to 
         the hospital in a rickshaw by those two persons, but I do not find any 
         statement of any rickshaw driver in the papers of the investigation. In 
         any view of the matter, the case is not free from doubt. The father is
Page 3 of 4
HC-NIC                                        Page 3 of 4      Created On Sat Jan 23 01:53:26 IST 2016

         running from the pillar to post for justice. He feels that the Investigating
